owner: W1-17. RI-DLG01 §How-we-lose: 'there is no Balmora, no outlander, no bad dreams, no lore node that pays nothing and exists only because the world does.' This file is those nodes.

infos.x: Learn the wamasu before it learns you. Friend, that is not a joke.
This one also carries letters. Cheap. Friend, and this one reads none of them.

I was a boat-hand and then I was a boat-hand with one arm, dry-one, and the province has no work at all for a boat-hand with one arm, and I have had eleven years to think about how quickly that happened.
Things that bite. Things that wait. Friend, the second sort is worse. Where are you walking?
The provincial bestiary runs to four hundred entries. Roughly a third of them are, on inspection, the same animal at different ages. It was compiled from the reports of people who were running away.
It is not hunted and it is not driven off, supplicant, it is walked around, and a village that cannot walk around a wamasu has built itself in the wrong place.
Long. Slow. Then not slow. Friend, it carries lightning in the skin. Have you seen one?
Hides in the mud. Shell like a boat. Friend, step on one once and you will step carefully forever.
They come down on the boards for anything left out, dry-one, and they aren't frightened of a person at all. I've had one take bread out of my hand.
Carrion bird. Follows the column. Bad omen, the men say. It is just a bird.
Good eating. Bad temper. Friend, take the claws first. Do you cook?
A creature with no fixed form that digests by contact, and it is generally encountered in flooded interiors. No sale catalogue of xanmeer material has ever mentioned it.
In the deep channels. Not often. Friend, once is enough.

It is not a creature and it is not a made thing, supplicant; it is a piece of a root that has been asked to stand up, and it is put down again when the asking stops, and the asking is not always ours.
Every pot on one fire at the turn of the season, dry-one. A person with nothing can put in a handful of weed and take out a bowl, and not a word is said. It has never been written down anywhere.
Crab, eel, root-bread, salt fish. And rice where the Empire got the fields in, friend. What are you after?
It's grey, it's heavy, and it doesn't go off for a week, dry-one. I've been given it in nine settlements and it's been the same bread in all nine. I've grown fond of it, in a way I can't explain.
Off the Morrowind border. Four a year. Shut the gate. And don't breathe it!
The storms are Morrowind's and arrive here diminished. The Office records them as a meteorological nuisance. The border villages stopped planting the north slope thirty years ago.

It isn't the vat cough and it isn't the fever, dry-one. It's a third thing that comes off the border and goes when the wind changes. And the physicians treat all three the same way, because they have one draught and it is for coughs.
Four months. No carts. Friend, this one drinks. Will you be here for it?

Cut into every doorpost in the low country with the year beside them, and read as a series they are the most reliable climatic record in the province and are three centuries longer than anything the Office holds.
Flat, poled, no keel. Friend, they go where a cart can't, and they sink where a cart wouldn't.
Four families run the river. Licensed. Fee to the Office. Mostly they honour it.
A drake a letter, town to town. Friend, faster than the Office and only slightly less honest.
They are not songs in the sense you mean and they are not sung to the tree, supplicant, they are sung at the same time as the tree, and the difference is the entire theology.
A clutch is tended by whoever is nearest and belongs to no one, and an outsider hears that as neglect until they notice that a thing which belongs to no one cannot be sold.
Not the great fever. The ordinary one, dry-one. We've all had it twice and it isn't counted. It takes one child in six. The chapel at Soulrest buried nine last winter.
It is given to the dying and to the newly named and to no one else, and what it does is not healing, supplicant, it is that the tree is asked to hold something for a while.

A thing given to the root is kept by the root and can be asked for again, and the asking is the difficult part, and there are keepers who have spent forty years learning to ask and have not been answered.

The Imperial gloss is ancestor worship, and the practice as described to me by three keepers is not worship and does not concern ancestors; it concerns storage, and the distinction has never made it into a single document in the annexe.

What is left of a death that was not returned. It is not a ghost and it is not a soul, and both of those words have been put on it by people who needed it to be one of the things they already had a word for.
Gems. Small ones. Friend, this one does not carry those and does not ask who does.

It is the worst of the offences and it is the only one the Empire has a word for, and so it is the only one that is ever prosecuted, and every keeper in this province has an opinion about what that arrangement has done to us.
There is no guild here and the Office has never been able to establish who instructs whom. That is not an absence of practitioners. The training arrangement simply does not resemble a school.

There's a woman on the Clay Moor who'll teach a stranger anything for a week's food, dry-one. And there's a man at Lilmoth who won't teach at any price. Between them, that's all the instruction in the province.
Fourteen built. Three garrisoned. The rest are stone and frogs. Were you looking for one in particular?

Imperial milestones survive along the southern trunk and give distances to a place that is not on any current map. It is generally taken as a corruption of a name. I now believe it is a settlement that was removed from the register rather than from the ground.

The name has been struck from the register in the same hand throughout, on thirty separate sheets. A clerk correcting an error does not do that. An instruction was carried out, and instructions of that kind are minuted somewhere. I would like to find the minute.
The great crabs on the coast road. Six passengers. Slow, friend, but you arrive dry. Are you taking one?
Fixed by the Office. Posted at the station. And the posted fare isn't what you pay.

Members of certain houses are moved between certain halls by an arrangement which the Office declines to describe and taxes at a flat rate, and the flat rate is the only reason anyone outside those houses knows the arrangement exists.

The practice of setting a place in the mind and returning to it is attested, is not taught in this province, and is subject to the same two limits everywhere it is attested: it will not carry you underground and it will not carry you out of a fight.
A supplicant who is lost may be brought to the nearest well, and it is the well that does the bringing, and it has never once brought anyone anywhere they were not already expected.
They are older than the roads they are on and the roads were laid to reach them, supplicant, whatever the survey says about the order of it.

There are fires that never go out at the crossings, and any traveller may sit at one, dry-one. No one owns them. No one tends them. And they haven't gone out in my lifetime. I've decided not to think about it too hard.
Drakes here, septims north, shells in the deep marsh. Friend, this one takes all three and prefers the first. What have you got?

A stranger is not unwelcome, supplicant, a stranger is unplaced, and the entire difficulty is that the Empire has never understood that those are different problems and has spent two centuries apologising for the wrong one.
All of us are from somewhere. Friend, this one has been to most of them.
I've been called it, and I've called other people it, dry-one. The second time was worse. And I haven't done it since.

The word is generally translated assimilated and is more nearly rendered salted, and it is applied by interior Argonians to coastal ones with a precision and a cruelty that the Imperial ear entirely fails to register.
They are not hated, supplicant, they are owed, and a debt is a much more durable arrangement than a hatred and does not tire.
If you are asking whether I am safe here, provincial, the answer is that I have been safe here for thirty years and have never once been welcome, and I find I can live with the arrangement.
They keep the covenant differently and they keep it, and the coast calls them animals for the difference, and the coast has forgotten which of the two of us was here when the other arrived.
River crews. Coast raiders. Not our jurisdiction and not their law either. Keep off the water after dark!
No cart goes. No boat stops. Friend, this one has nothing else on it. Are you thinking of going?
The region is named for a structure that has never been surveyed and that every account describes identically. Independent accounts of an unsurveyed thing normally diverge. These do not.
Mountains. Snow, even. I didn't believe it till I'd seen it. Have you been up?
West water. Warm. Full of boats. Friend, that is where the money comes in.
The eastern ocean. It is not a bay and does not behave like one. The weather it delivers is why Archon and Lilmoth build differently for what is nominally the same climate.
Wet, rich, crowded. Friend, Lilmoth and Blackrose both. Two very different towns on one soil.
Needles as far as a person can see and one path through them, dry-one, and the Empire has never taken it because there is nothing at the end of it but Thorn.
Dry rock. Salt. Bones. Friend, Soulrest is out there and not much else.

Cyrodiilic is the language of every instrument in force here and is spoken by perhaps a fifth of the population. Four fifths of this province is governed in a language it does not read. The Office regards that as an educational problem.
Sealed. Names you. Names your road. Show it at every gate. Have you got yours on you?
A curfew's a law about beds, dry-one, and it's enforced hardest on the people who haven't got one. I've stopped asking whether that is an accident.
Fourth bell in the garrison towns. Off the street. No exceptions, citizen — move along!
Above the tide line it has an owner. Below it, none. Friend, the fish are below it.
At every ford that has no boards. Friend, they set the price when you're halfway across. How much did they take off you?

An Imperial chapel of the first colonial period, now standing in four feet of water, still consecrated, and used by none except the swimmers, who are not of that faith and have never explained why they go in.
The chapel down there still has its bell, and it goes at the spring tide, dry-one. The Cohort says it's the current. But I've listened to a current for thirty years, and a current doesn't keep time.

You are asking whether the living gods of Morrowind are worshipped in this province. They are worshipped by four hundred Dunmer in six estates and by no one else. It has never troubled them. Why do you ask, provincial?
Chapels at Gideon, Stormhold and Blackrose, and attendance figures that the Imperial Cult reports as encouraging and that anyone who has stood at the back of one would report differently.

The body is returned to the ground the well is in, and where there is no well there is now an argument, and the argument at Soulrest has been running for two generations and has been settled by each house separately.
Heard at night from the interior. Not signals. Friend, this one asked once and was told they were counting.
Green, low, over the water, and every child is told they are gas and every adult still stops walking when one crosses the path, dry-one, and I have never met a soul who could tell me why they stop.

Once a year the water comes further than it should and everything below the mark is given up without argument, and it is the one day in the calendar when the coast keeps the covenant without being asked.

A keeper counts what a well has given and what it has been given, in hands, and the two columns are read aloud at the year's end in front of all who drew from it, and a village where the columns do not meet knows exactly whose fault it is.
Six years of less sap every year. Friend, this one is not a keeper and even this one can count.
The fish went first and nothing was made of it because fish move, dry-one, and then the wells started and now people are putting the two together and going quiet about it.
